newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Indonesia warns EU to keep out of East Timor issue.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia warns EU to keep out of East Timor issue.

text.p: Indonesia urged the European Union on Monday not to interfere in the disputed territory of East Timor, a former Portuguese colony.

In a sharply worded letter to Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring, whose country is currently EU president, Indonesia's EU ambassador warned that European measures in East Timor could have "grave repercussions".
"The advocacy of the European Union for concrete proposals could have grave consequences that could exacerbate, rather than serve, the cause of East Timor," Poedji Koentarso wrote.

The ambassador said that any EU proposals, which one Irish diplomat said would focus on development projects such as building primary schools, could jeopardize current tripartite talks on East Timor between Portugal, Indonesia and the United Nations.
"Outside interventions...may serve the interests of Portugal but undermine, with grave repercussions, the very principle of the talks," the letter said.

Koentarso also warned that EU intervention could "provoke extra-regional responses by EU external partners concerned about the peremptory ambitions of the Union's emerging common foreign and security policy".
At the General Affairs Council in Brussels, Portugal invited the European Commission to draw up concrete proposals for development aid to East Timor, which has a population of some 900,000.
In a brief statement, ministers expressed support for talks, scheduled to resume next month, between Portugal and Indonesia under U.N. auspices, and said they hoped there would be tangible progress.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and annexed it a year later in an act not recognised by the U.N., which still regards Lisbon as the territory's administering power.

Indonesia's military said earlier on Monday that armed opposition to Jakarta's rule in East Timor had dwindled from last year, citing a drop in the number of separatist guerrillas in the territory's rugged hills.
